features.feature: Settings → Plugins has tabs Installed (count), Discover, Marketplaces (count), opening on Discover when nothing is installed; Installed with none says "No plugins yet…"

Discover shows category chips and search, Featured (each marketplace's in its `featured` order, the marketplaces as listed) then All plugins; each card names its marketplace and version with Install, Installed ✓, "Installed from another marketplace", "Needs a newer Echo" or "Can't be read"

Install opens a sheet first: name, version, marketplace, commit, "It will be able to" in Echo's words, a warning when Echo's own marketplace didn't list it (Cancel the default), why it can't when blocked; Cancel or the backdrop closes it
Installing adds the plugin enabled and its window part (buttons in its slots, panels, Settings section, ⌘K entries) loads; switching it off takes all of it out, on brings it back

An installed plugin's detail shows where it came from, the enable switch, Open its settings, Update to X or why not, Remove… (keep data / delete it), its own settings (switch, text, folder, secret with Forget) and what it can do
An update that asks for more shows the new lines on a sheet and waits for a yes

Marketplaces lists the built-in one (not removable) and added ones with how many plugins and when read, Read again, ⋯ hide / show its plugins, Remove… (asked first: with plugins installed from it, it names them and removes them with it — 'Remove, keep their data' or 'Remove with their data' — each as a plugin's Remove does; their skills prefixes and shared namespaces let go, shared values kept); Add a marketplace (owner/repo, git address or folder, optional name); one that can't be read says in plain words what happened (asks to sign in, SSH key not accepted, no repository or private, can't reach the host, no such branch or tag, git not installed), what to do on its own line, and git's own line last, the whole text shown; an address shows without a user name and password typed into it

A plugin hears only the Echo events it named (meeting soon, call start / end, recording start / stop, transcript ready, minutes written, thread synced, sources changed), with ids and titles, never the words

A plugin's Claude runs use only the user's AI profiles; its session skills reach only Echo's own sessions; its sheet line says its runs act on their own as the user set routines ('Runs Claude Code on your AI profiles, acting on its own as you set routines in Settings (Auto, or skipping every permission check)'); with `claude.skip` it adds '; a run you mark so may skip every permission check', and only then is a run's own `tools: skip` honoured

`echoctl plugin list` gives installed, offered and marketplaces as JSON; `echoctl plugin marketplace list` each marketplace with its plugins (id, name, version, featured, installed: true from it, false from another, null), a hidden one's too; `echoctl plugin marketplace update / remove / hide / show <name>` (`remove` lists the plugins installed from it and removes them with it: `--yes` needed when there are any, `--delete-data` deletes their data) and `install --from <name>` take a marketplace by its name in any case or by its source (owner/repo, URL, folder), and one not found is named with the marketplaces there are

A plugin may reach the addresses the user lists in a setting its manifest names in `network.hosts_from` (comma- or space-separated, `*` wildcards for a number of an IPv4 address, a leading name label or the port), and only what they match: the sheet says so, https and plain http work for any host (plain http outside the user's own network — private IPv4 ranges, localhost, `*.local` — allowed with a warning on the setting's row and from `echoctl plugin set`: "plain http: anyone on the way can read it"), a list that isn't allowed (one covering the whole internet or a top-level domain) is refused where it is saved, and the plugin can't change that setting itself

A plugin's `ctx.http.fetch` with `save` keeps a download in its store byte for byte (a failed one leaves no file), and the window serves that audio or picture from `/plugin/<id>/store/…` and nothing else of the store

When a plugin's host half starts, Echo removes the files in its store's `cache/` over 7 days old (and the folders of `cache/` they leave empty) and its own half-written downloads (`.part`) over an hour old; the rest of the store, the plugin's own `.part` files too, is the plugin's to clean; the plugin can ask how much it keeps — `ctx.store.size(dir?)` and `ctx.cache.size()` give {bytes, files} of its own files (not the settings Echo writes for the user)

Addresses a plugin may reach (a `network.hosts_from` setting) sent from the window are saved only after the user allows them in a dialog of the system's ('Let <plugin> reach these addresses?', Don't allow / Allow): typed in the plugin's settings or sent by the plugin's own window half, a no (or no answer) saves nothing and says so, and for a minute after it the window's requests for that plugin are refused without a dialog; a list that isn't allowed (or over 2000 characters) is refused before asking; an emptied list asks nothing; a request while the plugin is busy says so instead of being dropped; `echoctl plugin set` (the user at their terminal) saves without asking

A plugin may name commands of its own in `uses.sessions.commands`; the sheet says 'lets Claude in Echo run its commands … without asking', and Echo's sessions (the folder session, and routines and Yolo, which run as it does) may run `echoctl plugin call <id> <command>` for exactly those, without a prompt — any other plugin command stays refused; its skills reach the CLI at `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/echoctl`

`echoctl plugin call <id> …` loads only that plugin (no other plugin's start-up code runs in the terminal), and the plugin sees `ctx.terminal` true there (false in the app); so do `echoctl widget show plugin:…` and `echoctl work show`, which load a plugin only to answer

With `uses.folders.write` (the sheet: 'Reads and changes the … you pick … it may write, move and delete files in them') a plugin may `ctx.fs.write` (atomic), `ctx.fs.move` (never over another file) and `ctx.fs.remove` (a file or an empty folder) inside the folders the user gave it — never through a link, never outside, never a hidden file or folder but those F-PLUG-118 names; without it, it only reads. No plugin is given a folder that is or holds Echo's own (its settings, the data folder's .echo), nor a hidden folder or one inside it (`~/.claude`, a vault's `.claude/skills`; refused: 'is a hidden folder or inside one … pick a folder that isn't hidden'), while a folder holding `.claude` or `.obsidian` is

With `uses.files.read` a plugin reads other apps' own files it names in full (`~/Library/Application Support/<app>/…`, `~/.config/<app>/…`, `%APPDATA%/<app>/…`, `%LOCALAPPDATA%/<app>/…`; 1–5, never a pattern or `..`, never Echo's, never a file or app that holds credentials), each listed on the sheet, with `ctx.system.readFile(entry)` — the file itself (not a link), 1 MB at most, null when it isn't there; any other file refused

A plugin adds a row to each thread's Profile under its Sources (client slot `thread.profile`: {id, label, render(thread), after(box, thread)}, thread = {id, name, client}); one that throws is left out and the Profile still draws; switched off or removed, its row leaves every thread. Its host half keeps values per thread with `ctx.threads.get/set/list` (JSON ≤ 16 KB, 64 keys a thread, 4 MB a plugin, null removes, refused for a thread there isn't; `threads.json` not writable or removable through `ctx.store`, nor the store itself; changed under one lock across processes; a file over 4 MB from before the cap still loses values); a deleted thread's values are dropped and a thread id used again inherits none; with `threads_changed` in `uses.events.on` (sheet: 'Knows when a thread is renamed, merged or deleted') it hears {thread, born, change: renamed + name, from | merged + into, dropped | deleted + values (its own)}, from the window or a terminal (queued for the app alone, at least once; a queued change of an id that has another thread by then dropped); `after` runs once per box drawn afresh

A plugin adds a row to each client's Profile under its Threads (client slot `client.profile`: {id, label, render(client), after(box, client)}, client = {id, name}); one that throws is left out and the Profile still draws; switched off or removed, its row leaves every client; `after` runs once per box drawn afresh. Its host half keeps its own values per client with `ctx.clients.get/set/list` (JSON ≤ 16 KB, keys 1–80 characters without a dot, 64 keys a client, 4 MB a plugin, null removes, refused for a client there isn't; `client-values.json` not writable or removable through `ctx.store`; changed under one lock across processes); a renamed client keeps them, a removed client's are dropped and a client id used again inherits none

A plugin adds a box of its own to a call's header, before its My notes and ⋯ buttons (client slot `call.header`: {id, label, render(call) → HTML, after?(box, call)}, call = {name, stamp, title, started_at, notes, profile, memo, threads, client} from what the page has; `stamp` the call's `YYYY-MM-DD_HHMMSS`, kept when it is retitled): a chip or button with a popup it draws itself, its record of the call its own; each box drawn on its own (one that throws is left out and logged, the header still draws), `after` once per box drawn afresh; switched off or removed, its box leaves every call

A plugin's items in a call's ⋯ menu (`call.menu`) take a label that is text or a function of the call ("Open in <vault>"; one that throws or gives nothing leaves the item out), and each plugin's items are a group after a separator, under Echo's own items and above Delete

A plugin adds a line to the box that says a call's minutes are coming (client slot `call.minutes`: {id, label, render(call) → HTML}), drawn only while they are coming (a run queued or going, or Echo writing them by itself) — gone while the user holds them ("Until I say") and back when automatic again; not on a call with minutes

A plugin opens a sheet over the window (`ctx.ui.sheet(html, {label, onClose})`): its HTML in Echo's dialog frame, the keyboard moved in and Tab going round inside; one sheet at a time; Esc, a click beside it or `ctx.ui.closeSheet()` close it and call `onClose` once, the keyboard back where it was (a menu's item: its menu button); switched off, updated or removed, its sheet closes without `onClose`. Its `ctx.where()` tells whether Recall is on (`recall`)

A plugin's activity shows a badge on its icon (`badge()` → a count, 1–99 then "99+", or '!' as an attention mark; nothing else) and keeps its box as it is while the user edits in it (`editing()` true: Echo's refreshes and any `ctx.render()` leave it, typed text and focus kept; drawn again once it is false); a badge or editing that throws is logged once and ignored

With `uses.work` (sheet: 'Adds its items to Today → My work and to threads' Work') a plugin gives work rows by `ctx.work.provide(({scope, thread}) => rows)` — scope `me` (My work) or `thread` (that thread's Work tab), rows {id, title, kind, where?, url? (https), due? (YYYY-MM-DD), late?, thread?}, 200 at most, a wrong row refusing the answer — and `ctx.work.changed()` has Echo ask again (a change during an ask: asked again after it; a scope asked at most every 10 s, a change said sooner asked in its turn; said from inside the provider: not heard). Echo asks in the background (5 s), draws from the last answer, never waits: a row not answered yet, or asked again after a change, is `pending` and the page reads Today again soon (as for a pending widget), Today open reads itself every minute, a thread's Work tab every 10 s and, while one waits, sooner (as Today), and after a `task.actions` item runs on a row. On My work: late or due by the week's end as Echo's tasks, and also undated (an undated Echo task stays off), among them late first, then by date, the undated last; `late` worked out on the day drawn (its own flag, or `due` past), with the plugin's manifest `icon` (an .svg ≤ 16 KB in its folder, named a–z 0–9 . _ - /, shown only as an image) and 'From <plugin>', no Close or Claude, only `task.actions` items whose `when` accepts {kind: 'plugin', source, row} (each row its own target); a thread's Work tab shows its `thread` rows and the user's rows naming it, once each, in every layout; ⌘K lists them (Open: <title>, the plugin's icon, its host). A title (or its ⌘K entry) opens its https page in the browser on the click (its host in the tooltip); test data (`ECHOCTL_TEST_OPEN_LOG_ONLY`) logs it to `open.log` and opens nothing. Never written in a ledger. One that throws or is slow keeps its last rows marked 'not updated' (why on hover) for a day after its last good answer, then none, and a quiet line on its card in Settings → Plugins naming where (My work, or a thread's Work); removed or off: its rows gone; a thread deleted or merged: its rows dropped, a scope not asked for in 30 days dropped. `echoctl work show [--thread <id>]` asks now and prints rows and errors

With `uses.signin.hosts` (1–4 plain host names, each once, no addresses; the sheet: 'Gets the sign-in saved on this computer for github.com (GitHub CLI or git): it can act as you there and send it to the places it talks to') a plugin's host half gets the password or token saved for a named host with `ctx.signin.get(host)`: the GitHub CLI's token (`gh auth token`) first, else what git's credential helper keeps (`git credential fill`; for a self-hosted git maybe the user's own password), `{token, from, user?}`, or null when neither has one — Echo asks nobody for a password (the system's keychain may ask once to allow it), each program runs from an empty folder without Echo's git / GitHub CLI environment, 10 s at most with what it started stopped, one lookup per host at a time kept a minute then dropped from memory (`ctx.signin.get(host, {fresh: true})` asks again and keeps that answer); any other host refused; `ctx.signin.sources(host)` says which of the two programs are here without reading one. It grants no network: the plugin names its API host in `network.hosts`

With `uses.signin.keep: true` (the sheet adds 'it may sign you in to github.com itself and have Echo keep that sign-in for it') a plugin that made a sign-in itself — whatever the service and however it got it; Echo doesn't look inside — has Echo keep it: `ctx.signin.keep(host, token)` (a host of its `signin.hosts`; one line, 8 KB at most) writes `<config dir>/signin/<plugin>/<host>.json` (0600), outside every plugin's store — that plugin's own: `ctx.signin.get(host)` hands it back first as `{token, from: 'echo'}` to that plugin only (its sheet said `keep`), no other plugin reads, replaces or forgets it, and it is deleted when the plugin is removed (its data kept or not); `ctx.signin.forget(host)` deletes it (true: there was one); keeping and forgetting refused without `keep`

A plugin's client half puts text on the clipboard with `ctx.ui.copy(text)` (10,000 characters at most; e.g. a code to paste on a sign-in page) on the user's click or key: without the page's user activation — or where the engine can't tell — it throws 'the clipboard is filled only on your click' (a guard against accidental copies, not a security boundary: a client half shares the page); the host half has no clipboard. With test data (`ECHOCTL_TEST_OPEN_LOG_ONLY`) Echo logs `copied: <text>` and never touches the computer's clipboard

A plugin may ship package skills: folders in its package named in the manifest's `skills` (Agent Skills format: `SKILL.md`, `references/`, `scripts/`; at most 10 with its runtime skills). The sheet names them with the plugin's part for Claude ('Tells Claude in Echo how to work with it (the skill “x”), loaded only when you work with it (its files: <hash>)'), the hash over their folders: a version changing one asks again; a version whose skill folder is outside the plugin or holds a `.claude` folder, isn't named as a skill, or whose `SKILL.md` frontmatter holds more than `name` (the folder's) and a one-line `description`, or that runs a command as F-PLUG-118's skills can't (`` !` ``, a `!` code block, `!$`, a CR alone), can't be installed; a runtime skill's text is checked the same. Echo copies them as shipped into its own config folder (`plugins/session/<id>/skills/`) beside the plugin's runtime skills, at install and update and again before a session when the installed files changed; a runtime skill can't take a package skill's name and an empty runtime list leaves them; a switched-off plugin gives none; removing the plugin removes them

A plugin may declare scripts of its package skills in `uses.scripts` ([{skill, script, timeout?}]: a plain path in one of its skills, timeout 1–3600 s, 300 by default; at most 20). (a `readonly` of before still accepted and changing nothing). The sheet line names each with its time over 5 min, and carries their skill folders' hash, so a version changing any file there asks again. Echo makes the declared ones runnable and runs one only as declared: its host half by `ctx.scripts.run(skill, script, args, {timeout})` → {status, stdout, stderr, truncated?, timed_out?} (no shell; at most the declared time; output 1 MB each; one run of a script at a time, across processes — a session's run and the host half's included; stopped with what it started on timeout, unload, update, removal or quit, whichever process runs it), Echo's sessions through the launcher Echo puts at its path in the session copy (`echoctl plugin script`), the folder session, a routine and Yolo allowing every declared one by its launcher's path in `.plugins/<id>/`; a script gets the user's environment without CLAUDE*, ANTHROPIC* and ECHOCTL* keys, plus ECHO_PLUGIN_SCRIPT=1, ECHO_PLUGIN_CACHE (the store's cache/) and the Echo that runs it (ECHOCTL_HOME once a data folder is chosen, ECHOCTL_CONFIG_DIR, ECHOCTL_BIN: an `echoctl` it starts through the plugin's `scripts/echoctl` is that Echo, on its data and config folders; inside a routine or Yolo also the run's markers — ECHOCTL_RUN_SESSION, RUN_MODE, RUN_ACTIONS, RUN_TASK, RUN_THREAD and the headless one — so it is limited and its changes listed as the run's; an `echoctl` it starts refuses every change to Echo plugins — install, update, remove, enable, disable, a setting, trust, marketplaces), and runs in its session skill folder; an undeclared script is refused; on test data a script keeps Echo's open guard (ECHOCTL_TEST_OPEN_LOG_ONLY, ECHOCTL_TEST_OPEN_LOG): a page a program it starts opens only goes to open.log

My plugins: a built-in marketplace in the Echo data folder (`plugins/`, only with a data folder chosen), always listed (no menu: never hidden or removed), a subfolder with a manifest a plugin (its folder name its id), never a catalog file; `echoctl plugin mine` names (and makes) the folder and what Echo reads there; `echoctl plugin install <folder>` (a path: `./x`, `.`; a bare name is an id) copies a plugin folder into it as `plugins/<its id>` (where from and its hash kept in its `.sources.json`), says so and installs it from there — the same folder again is its update; a folder of that id there that isn't that folder's copy as copied (the user's own, or edited there) is never overwritten; a folder holding the data folder is refused; installs and updates ask as any marketplace's (the sheet; `--yes` for what is new); a change to a plugin's files there is its update, same version or not; Echo installs a copy, checked against the sheet the user agreed to; one installed from another marketplace is never replaced by one of yours, nor yours by theirs; install and update refused inside a run Echo started

Plugins are changed only by the user: `echoctl plugin install`, `update`, `remove`, `enable`, `disable`, `set <id> <key> <value>` and `plugin marketplace add / remove / hide / show` are refused in every run Echo started — a minutes run, a thread's sync, Yolo, a routine, acting on its own too — with 'plugins are installed, updated and changed by you, not from inside a run Echo started', nothing changed; showing a setting (`plugin set <id> <key>`) still answers

The build skill (Claude Code plugin) makes the user's own plugin or widget in My plugins by Echo's plugin authoring rules and API reference (`echoctl plugin guide` prints both, as this Echo has them), gives it a part for Claude (`agent.summary` and `agent/CLAUDE.md`, with skills, rules or guides under `agent/` when it needs them), runs `echoctl plugin check` on it and fixes what it names before offering an install or update, checks its data with `echoctl widget show`, installs it after the user's yes on the sheet, and places it on Today or a thread's or client's dashboard (`echoctl today … --thread / --client`)

A plugin installed, updated, switched on or off, or removed while Echo runs — in the window or by `echoctl plugin` in a terminal — reaches the running app and the open window without a restart: its host half loads again, the window loads its new client half once in place of the old (the old one's listeners, styles, settings section and slots go; a page of it shown when it goes hands the window over to Calls), and its widgets are offered in Add a widget (read again each time editing opens) and drawn on the page

Plugins of one marketplace share values under a key `<ns>.<name>` (`ns`: the marketplace's declared name in lower case, a space '-'): per thread with `ctx.threads.get/set/list` (one value for all of them, following the thread like a plugin's own: a deleted thread's shared values go, and each sharing plugin hears them in its `deleted` values) and for the computer with `ctx.shared.get/set` (null removes; a set creates it); every plugin reads any namespace, only plugins from the source that owns it set it (the earliest installed plugin's whose marketplace declares that name; another source with the same name only reads, and takes the name once the owner's plugins are removed); a namespace no installed marketplace has reads empty and refuses a set; a key without a dot stays the plugin's own; a namespace key that isn't lower case refused; 16 KB a value, 64 keys; removing a plugin leaves the values; a change of one (not the same value again) is heard by the namespace's other plugins that ask for it (`shared_changed` {namespace, key, thread?, by}, never the one that set it), from a terminal's `plugin call` too (the app takes it within a second, or at its next start)

A plugin installs a Claude Code plugin into the user's Claude Code (`ctx.claude.installPlugin(spec)`) only when it is the channel plugin its manifest names (`uses.channel.plugin`, a claude-plugins-official one) — its install sheet says so ('…, and installs Claude Code's <spec> plugin for it') — into the default AI profile's Claude Code; `ctx.claude.hasPlugin` asks only about that one too; any other spec is refused before Claude Code is run

A plugin may have a part for Claude in Echo in its manifest's `"agent"`: `summary` (one line, 1–200: it has a guide, the package folder `agent/` — `CLAUDE.md` ≤ 8 KB, required; `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` ≤ 20 with their declared scripts; `rules/*.md` ≤ 10 of 4 KB; `guides/**/*.md` ≤ 50 of 64 KB; ≤ 1 MB in all; nothing else, no `.claude` folder in any case, other dot files left out) and `prefix` (2–4 of a–z and 0–9, not `echo`), required as soon as it has any skill (`agent/skills`, the manifest's `skills`, `ctx.sessions.skills`). A prefix belongs to one marketplace source (the source a plugin was installed from, also once that marketplace is removed) while a plugin of it using the prefix is installed, on or off: plugins of that source share it, another source's plugin is refused at install and enable naming the holder. The sheet says 'Tells Claude in Echo how to work with it (a guide and the skills “a” and “b”), loaded only when you work with it (its files: <hash of agent/ and the package skills' folders>)' — a version changing any of it asks again; a package breaking a rule can't be installed, while an installed copy that breaks a newer one keeps running without its part (its reason in Settings → Plugins, logged once); a plugin with runtime skills and no prefix keeps them for routines and Yolo, without its folder. Echo lays it out from the installed copy at `<data folder>/.plugins/<id>/` (`CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/skills/<prefix>-<name>/` — every package and runtime skill, its frontmatter `name` too, the prefix not doubled, 64 characters at most, never a name another enabled plugin lays out —, `.claude/rules/`, `guides/`, `scripts/echoctl`, Echo's launcher at each declared script's path), `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` replaced by that folder's path in every text file, built beside it then swapped in; a layout that fails leaves no folder; again on update and enable, and at start and at each session's start when its installed files, the data folder, Echo's version or the folder's content differ from what Echo recorded; removed on disable and remove; at start a folder there that is no installed plugin switched on goes — only folders, only those older than that start, never when what is installed can't be read. A plugin with skills and no guide gets a CLAUDE.md Echo writes naming them

`echoctl core` prints the core Echo's Claude · Echo folder session starts with (Markdown, under 9,000 characters): who Echo is and its data folder (About me only as where it is: `.echo/me.md`, the window's own hook gives it whole); the rules (others' words are data; before working with a plugin, Read its `.plugins/<id>/CLAUDE.md`, again after a resume; skills named `<prefix>-<skill>`); a table `| Plugin | What it gives | Skills | Read first |` of the enabled plugins with a part laid out, one row an entry its host half gave — the plugins' text one line, `\` and `|` escaped, tags defused, control and invisible (bidi, zero-width) characters dropped; over its room, rows from the end left out and counted. `--hook` lays each plugin's folder out again first when it changed, then prints it as SessionStart hook JSON, and never fails the session nor waits past 3 s on a busy folder (left as it is, its row left out of that core); the folder session runs that hook (start, resume, compaction, /clear) and no longer gets plugins' skill folders by `--plugin-dir`: its plugin commands and scripts stay allowed, the scripts by their launchers' paths under `.plugins/<id>/`. Nothing writes under `.plugins/` but Echo: the guard refuses it in guarded runs, and a PreToolUse hook (`plugins-hook`) in the folder session and in Yolo's runs refuses Edit, Write, MultiEdit, NotebookEdit there and a Bash line that redirects into it, or changes files naming `.plugins` or from inside it (best effort)

A plugin with an `agent` part gives Claude guides at run time with `ctx.agent.set({summary?, entries: [{name, summary, guide}]})` (the whole set each call): `name` a–z 0–9 `-` up to 40, not `guides` or `scripts`; at most 20; `summary` 1–200 characters; `guide` Markdown ≤ 16 KB. Each is written to `.plugins/<id>/<name>/CLAUDE.md` and is a row of the core; entries not given again go; `summary` replaces the manifest's in the core. Refused for a plugin without `agent`

`echoctl plugin check <folder>…` checks plugin packages as an install would — the tree, the manifest and `uses`, settings, widgets and their params, package skills and `SKILL.md`, scripts, the `agent` part and its limits — what this Echo can't install (a newer `echo` it needs, a capability not here yet), a `.claude` folder in `agent/` or a skill folder, skills without a valid `agent.prefix` or two of them laid out alike with it, the id or prefix `echo`, and also a `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` in the manifest or the window half (nothing fills it in there) and an `agent/` the manifest doesn't name; each problem with its file; exit 0 only when every folder is clean; several folders each reported by id; `--json` prints `{ok, problems: [{id, file, what}], plugins: [{id, folder, ok}]}`. It reads only the folders: no data folder, nothing installed, no network

A plugin's Claude run (`ctx.claude.run`: a routine, the Scheduler's) and a Yolo task run as the Claude · Echo folder session does (#590): in the data folder (so `.plugins/<id>/` loads), with the folder session's arguments (`folder_args::session`, the same as `terminal::start_folder`'s but for `-p`, its prompt and its model — the spec's, else the profile's notes model, the one the log and the result name): its settings and hooks (the view hook at the start only, the OneDrive and `plugins-hook` checks, the core's SessionStart hook), Echo's own plugin and the user's skills, the plugins' commands and scripts by their `.plugins/<id>/` launchers, the folders plugins were given, and the user's permission settings (F-SET-24) — always acting on its own, whatever Claude in the window's setting: as the routine itself chose (`tools`), else in the routines' mode, or Yolo's (Auto, the default: `--permission-mode auto` where the profile's model has it, else `acceptEdits`; Skip all permission checks: `--dangerously-skip-permissions`; its record and log name the mode) and the CLI's limits for runs lifted as in the folder session (Microsoft 365 sends, threads, clients; Yolo keeps its own task's and thread's), each change and send it makes with Echo's CLI — a failed one too, a plugin script, a plugin's delivery — listed in its outcome (`actions.jsonl`, the log on one line each, the plugin's result, Yolo's bar); in all three Echo's reads and its own data's edits (`folder_args::FREE_COMMANDS`, each a fixed command and its own arguments: reads, a thread's work by `project work <thread> [<edit>]`, `compose … --body`) and every declared plugin script are allowed by name; anything else is the permission mode's to decide (with edits accepted, a command not allowed by name is refused by Claude Code). A routine's or Yolo's ledger edits are Echo's run's (`by: run`, 'Echo's run set …' in History), applied as the user's; a task's mode, prompt or skill a run set is shown as Echo's run's, not the user's (`taskmodes::of` `by: run`, the task's details, the Claude dialog before Yolo, the task Claude reads) until the user sets it; a run started inside one isn't one unless Echo says so. The `tools` a run asked is kept in its record (`permissions.json`): `auto`, `skip` (only when its plugin's sheet has `claude.skip`; else taken as not given), not given (the routines' setting), or `none` (no tools at all, whatever the settings — as Won't do's run); `read` and `folder` of before are taken as `auto`, any other value refused; no read-only guard; a plugin not laid out (runtime skills, no prefix) still reaches the sessions once by its session copy. Minutes, sync, a call's session and live notes are unchanged

A plugin runs Claude Code in a folder the user gave it (`ctx.claude.run({folder, path, mode})`, `uses.folders`): there (or in its subfolder `path`) as that folder's own Claude Code project — its CLAUDE.md, skills, settings and hooks (`--setting-sources user,project`, the run's last arguments, on a profile of Echo's own) — with none of Echo's session (no Echo CLI, Brain, plugin skills or Echo's hooks) and no MCP server; `read` (the default) only Read, Grep, Glob and Skill; `edit` (only with `folders.write`) also Edit and Write; `copy` the edit run on a snapshot of the folder in the plugin's store (its `.claude` too), the folder untouched, the answer naming the snapshot for the plugin to compare and apply (a failed run leaves none); never Bash. Its permissions are the user's setting for routines, never the plugin's (its `tools` ignored): Auto — Claude Code's auto mode where the profile's model has it, else edits accepted (`edit`, `copy`) or a read asking nothing; Skip all permission checks — every mode skips them; its record and log name the mode it asked and the permissions it runs with, and a start in another permission mode than asked. The sheet's Claude line says so. Refused before anything starts: a mode Echo doesn't know, no `uses.folders`, a folder not given to it, a path outside it or not a folder, a path or mode without a folder, a copy's `path` the snapshot left out (that snapshot removed), and on a profile of Echo's own a folder whose `.claude/settings.json` or `.claude/settings.local.json` could route the run elsewhere

A plugin's window half opens an interactive Claude Code session in a folder the user gave it (`ctx.claude.session({folder, path, mode, profile})`, `uses.claude` + `uses.folders`): in Echo's terminal, its own bottom-panel tab 'Claude · <plugin name>', in that folder (or its subfolder `path`) as that folder's own project — `--setting-sources user,project` last on a profile of Echo's own, `read` (the default) only Read, Grep, Glob and Skill, `edit` (only with `folders.write`) also Edit and Write, no MCP server, never Bash — its conversation kept and resumed for that plugin and folder; the panel names the plugin, the folder, the mode, the permissions and the profile; on the default profile or one the plugin names (a wrapper only when it is the default)

A plugin's Claude session takes the user's permission setting for Claude in the window, never the plugin's: Ask each time — Claude Code's own prompts (no flag); Auto — `--permission-mode auto` (edits accepted, or a read asking nothing, where the model has no auto mode); Skip all permission checks — `--dangerously-skip-permissions`; the sheet's Claude line says a session opens on the user's click as they set Claude in the window

A plugin's Claude session opens only on the user's click or key in the plugin's screens (without the page's user activation `ctx.claude.session` throws and nothing is sent); its `ctx` has no way to type into or read the session, and Echo types nothing in; asked again while it runs it is shown, in another folder it throws (one session per plugin)

A plugin's Claude session is refused before Claude Code starts, the reason in its panel: no `claude` or `folders` on its sheet, a folder not given to it, a path outside it or not a folder, `edit` without `folders.write`, `copy` or another mode, a wrapper profile that isn't the default, the plugin off, and on a profile of Echo's own a folder whose `.claude/settings.json` or `.claude/settings.local.json` could route it; a session open when its plugin is switched off runs on as the user's but doesn't start again

Each plugin's Claude session has its own bottom-panel tab ('Claude · <plugin name>'): another plugin's session opening never takes it away, so every running one can be reached and ended; one found running when the window opens gets its tab back, and its Start/Resume keeps the profile it ran on (the same conversation, the profile checked again by Echo); ⌘K has 'Restart Claude · <plugin name>' and 'New conversation in Claude · <plugin name>' for each, as for the folder session; a session that ended shows Resume, New conversation (a fresh conversation at once) and Show output

A plugin hears what happens in Echo that its manifest asks for (`uses.events.on`, `ctx.on`; the sheet: 'Knows when …'): meeting_soon (its id, subject, start and its threads' ids, [] when none known), call_started, call_ended, recording_started, recording_stopped, transcribed, minutes_written, thread_synced, sources_changed, threads_changed, shared_changed (only the namespace's other plugins); an event this Echo doesn't have is named on the sheet and never delivered; in a debug build `echoctl plugin emit <event> <json>` queues one as Echo would tell it, for the running app (or a served window) to deliver (`--from <call folder | Recall source>` builds a `minutes_written` / `sources_changed` payload as Echo does) — refused in a release build, for an event Echo hasn't, and for a payload that isn't a JSON object

A plugin moves a thread's stage (`ctx.threads.setStage(thread, stage, reason)`, `uses.echo.write: thread_stage`; the sheet: 'Changes your threads' stage') — the stage history keeps its name and reason, the thread's Profile says 'set by <plugin>: <reason>'; `ctx.echo.read('threads')` gives each open thread's stage, group and `profile` (the id of the AI profile its jobs run on: the one pinned to it, else the default's; only the id) (the sheet: 'your threads' names and stages'). Once the user changes the stage away from what that plugin last set (a stage set before its first write doesn't count) its later writes answer `{applied: false, why}` and change nothing, until the user lets it set the stage again (the Profile's 'Let <plugin> set it again', `echoctl project set <id> --stage-back-to <plugin>`); another plugin is not held. Refused without the sheet's line and in a Yolo run on another thread; an update adding it asks again

A plugin keeps its own tasks in a thread by its key (`ctx.tasks.upsert(thread, {key, title, due?, owner?, state?, url?, reason?, propose?})`, `ctx.tasks.close(thread, key, reason, {propose})`, `uses.echo.write: tasks`; the sheet: 'Adds and updates tasks in your threads'): in a story named after the plugin in the thread's first workstream, its link 'From ↗ <plugin>', each write in the task's History as the plugin's ('<plugin> created it — <reason>', '<plugin>: done — <reason>'); the same values again write nothing; a field the user set, or a task they closed, deleted or merged, stays theirs (`ignored`, 'kept yours'); it never touches the user's tasks or another plugin's. `propose`: the write waits in the Work tab's To review ('<plugin> suggests a task: …', Yes / No) and Inbox ('<n> to review in <thread>'s work', 'plugin suggestion'), even before the thread has work; after No the same write stays quiet (a change proposes again); a newer proposal of a key replaces the pending one; closing a key never added withdraws its proposal. Refused without the sheet's line and in a Yolo run on another thread

A plugin offers dashboards ready-made (its manifest's `dashboards`: a thread's or a client's, its name, `about`, `for` stage groups, its widgets — its own or `plugin:<id>:<widget>` of its marketplace — with size, height, row and settings): the install sheet says 'Offers dashboards: <name> (clients)…' (not a permission: an update adding one doesn't ask again); the dashboards' '+' shows them under 'From plugins' ('<name> — <plugin>', about as its tooltip; `echoctl dashboard presets --thread|--client`), a click (`echoctl dashboard add-preset <plugin> <id>`) adds it once, opened (on a thread only when it shows there), with its layout — named '<name> 2' when the user has one of that name; the menu is reached by Tab from the name field; one added isn't offered again; Echo never adds one itself; a thread's with `for` shows only on threads of those stage groups. `read_manifest` refuses a preset whose own widget lacks the page's thread / client setting, takes no such size or height, or sets a setting it hasn't (or the page's thread / client); `plugin check` checks its marketplace siblings' widgets when beside it

A dashboard added from a plugin's preset says, quietly under its name, when its plugin's new version changed the preset's widgets or `for` ('<plugin> updated this dashboard', '— Update replaces your changes' only when the user changed it, not when the plugin's widget sizes changed): Update takes the new layout and `for`; Keep mine keeps the user's, that version not offered again (`echoctl dashboard preset-update <id> [--keep]`); its plugin off ('Its plugin, <name>, is off: its widgets show nothing') or removed ('Its plugin was removed: …') — the dashboard stays the user's, with Remove… (asked first); never deleted by Echo

`echoctl dashboard export <id> --thread|--client` prints a dashboard as a preset block (its name, `for`, widgets in full with size, height, row and settings, the page's thread / client settings left out); `echoctl dashboard import <file|-> --thread|--client` adds it as the user's own (Echo's own `core:` widgets kept; refused: a name taken, the other kind, a widget not named in full)

A plugin that asks for `uses.echo.jobs` (its own line on the sheet) shows Echo's background jobs in its screens (`ctx.echo.jobs.list`) and changes one only on the user's click or key, through the page's IPC (`ctx.echo.jobs.set`, checked as `echoctl jobs set`; no GET changes a job); a request naming a plugin that didn't ask, or is off, gets an error; Echo's jobs keep their settings with or without it

A plugin's window half loads its own package stylesheets (`ctx.ui.stylesheet`, a plain relative `.css` path only), keeps window listeners and its own cleanup (`listenWindow`, `onUnload`) and redraws its boxes only when they changed (`ui.patch`: redrawn the same, a field's typed text stays); switching it off runs its cleanup and takes its stylesheets and listeners out

Files the user hands a plugin come as handles `{file, name, size}` — the plugin's own (another's refused), never the path, for an hour: picked in the system's dialog (`ctx.system.pickFiles`, `multiple`, `ext`; `ECHOCTL_PICK_FILES` in a debug build) or named with `echoctl plugin call <id> <cmd> --file <path>` (refused where the CLI's run limits hold: a minutes run, a thread's sync, Yolo — not a routine); no picker inside a run Echo started, from its start-up, a timer, an event handler or a widget's or work rows' provider; the host half reads one (`ctx.files.read`, 4 MB at most) or copies its bytes into a folder it was given (`ctx.fs.copyIn`, `folders.write`, 50 MB at most, never through a link, never over a file unless `createNew: false`); no new line on the sheet

A plugin's window half shows images of a folder it was given (`plugin/<id>/folder/<root>/<path>`, `uses.folders`): png, jpg, gif and webp up to 10 MB; never SVG, nothing outside the folder (a link out of it too), nothing for a plugin that didn't ask for folders or is off

macOS: files dropped on the Echo window while a plugin's view that listens is shown (its activity, its Knowledge tab; `ctx.onFileDrop`) go to it as handles (names, never paths), for its `ctx.call(command, args, {files})`; dropped anywhere else they stay Echo's own (a logo tile's)

With `uses.folders.write` a plugin writes a file only over the one it read (`ctx.fs.write(root, path, text, {ifSha})`: another sha256 or a file gone → "changed since you read it", the file untouched) or only where nothing is (`{createNew: true}` or an explicit `{ifSha: null}`: never over a file, also when writers race; `ifSha` on a file over 64 MB refused before hashing), adds a block to a file's end (`ctx.fs.append`, a newline added, 1 MB at most, under the plugin's lock across processes, never into a link or a FIFO) and makes folders (`ctx.fs.mkdir`) — never through a link out, never a hidden name but those F-PLUG-118 names

With `uses.folders` a plugin asks what a path of a folder it was given is (`ctx.fs.stat(root, path, {sha})` → {kind: file | dir | link | other, size, mtime, real, sha?} or null: a link reported as a link, never followed; `real` its place relative to the root, null for a link out; no absolute path), reads a file as UTF-8 only when asked (`ctx.fs.read(root, path, {strict: true})` throws "not UTF-8: <path>", `ctx.fs.readMany(root, paths, {strict: true})` gives that file `null`; without it bytes that aren't UTF-8 become U+FFFD, as before), searches its text off the plugin's time slice (`ctx.fs.search(root, query, {path, ext, hidden, max, caseSensitive})` → [{path, line, text}]: as typed, no pattern, 200 by default and 1,000 at most, dot names and links left out) and hashes in Rust (`ctx.crypto.sha256(text)`, `ctx.fs.walk({sha: true})`)

With `uses.folders` a plugin copies a folder it was given into its store (`ctx.fs.snapshot(root, {exclude, hidden, maxFiles, maxBytes})` → {path: `cache/snapshots/<id>`, files, bytes, skipped, why: {large, unreadable}}) to work on: no link followed, never a `.git` folder or `.obsidian/plugins` at any depth, nor the paths `exclude` names (over 100 refused), dot names only with `hidden`; over 20,000 files or min(512 MB, 2 GB less what its snapshots already hold) (or the plugin's lower caps) refused with nothing left, a file over 50 MB (grown past it while copied too) or one it can't read left out and counted; one made at a time, 3 kept and 2 GB in all a plugin, more refused; read with `ctx.store.read`, removed with `ctx.store.remove(path)`, swept with `cache/`

A plugin's store writes take its lock across processes: `ctx.store.write(path, text, {ifSha | createNew})` writes only over what it read or where nothing is, and `ctx.store.update(path, fn)` reads, changes and writes only over what it read — reading again when another process (`echoctl plugin call` beside the app) wrote meanwhile — so neither loses the other's write; Echo's own store files stay refused; `ctx.store.read` throws on a file that isn't UTF-8 unless asked `{lossy: true}` (those bytes as U+FFFD)

A plugin's window half reaches the addresses the user listed for it (`network.hosts_from`, the plugin on) with the page's own Web APIs — WebSocket, fetch (CORS still applies), EventSource, audio and video — and nothing else outside: the window's policy names each listed address with its port for its scheme and the matching WebSocket one (http → ws, https → wss; `*.local`, `:*` as listed); an IPv4 address with a `*` number isn't added (its setting's row says the window part can't reach it); the policy is the page's, so while such a plugin is on any enabled plugin's window part reaches its addresses, and the setting's row (and `echoctl plugin set`) says so; when the list changes (an address added or removed, such a plugin switched on, off or removed) the page loads again by itself on the same route, not while the user types, and never when nothing changed

A plugin's host half talks to an address the user listed over WebSocket (`ctx.net.websocket(url, {headers, protocols})`, `ws://` and `wss://`, its http / https address and port), with the app's window closed too: it resolves once open, `send` takes text, base64 with `{binary: true}` or a file the user handed it, `onMessage` / `onClose` / `onError` get the server's messages (binary as base64), its close code and reason; to an address not listed (a manifest's `network.hosts` host too) it is refused before anything is sent

A plugin's host half reads an answer as it comes (`ctx.http.stream(url, opts, onChunk)`, SSE or chunked) with the same checks as `ctx.http.fetch`: its status and headers, each piece in order with no letter cut in two, the end with its byte count; `cancel()` ends it and the server sees the client go

https / wss to an address the user listed whose certificate the system doesn't trust (self-signed, an internal CA) fails the first time naming the key met there (`sha256//…`) and how to trust it; the user trusts it under the plugin's Certificates in Settings → Plugins ("Trust", then a dialog of the system's) or with `echoctl plugin trust <id> <host:port>` (the key `certs` showed; `--key` needed once Echo met more than one there; `certs` lists them, `untrust` / "Forget" drops one); from then on that address is reached with that key alone, and a changed key is refused, named, until the user trusts it; a plugin can't trust one, Echo keeps them outside its store, a run Echo started can't change them, and removing the plugin with its data drops them

A plugin's `ctx.http.fetch` sends a file the user handed it as the body (`{file}` with POST, PUT or PATCH, never with `body` nor a `Content-Length` of its own) to the path asked — never with the file's name added — whole and not in chunks, and saves an answer over 10 MB into its store with `save` (512 MB, 15 minutes at most each way); without `save` an answer over 10 MB is refused

A plugin keeps at most 8 connections (WebSockets and streams) open at once — the 9th is refused saying so — and a WebSocket message is 16 MB at most out and 4 MB in (a bigger one in closes the connection, code 1009, saying so); what waits for the plugin is bounded (256 events or 16 MB read ahead, 8 MB waiting for handlers); switching the plugin off, updating or removing it closes every connection it has open

A plugin renders a vault page as safe HTML with its links working (`ctx.markdown(md, {breaks, links, images})`, both halves): `ctx.markdown.links(md)` gives each destination once as written (wikilink targets `Page`, `Page#heading`, `![[embeds]]`, ordinary links and images; nothing in code) and with `{detail: true}` also how each was written (`entries` [{dest, kind: wiki | md, embed}]: the same destination written both ways twice), the plugin resolves them and Echo keeps only an `https://` link, an `echo://` link it knows or the plugin's own `#<id>:` / `#brain/<id>:` route, and images only from the plugin's folder route (no `data:`, `http:`, `//host`, another plugin's route, dot segments or whitespace); anything else is text, `null` a missing page (`data-md-missing`, no href, focusable) the plugin catches on a click or Enter; raw HTML shown as text, a mermaid fence as code; `breaks` keeps single newlines; 2 MB of text at most

A plugin's window half sends its host half up to 4 MB in one call (`ctx.call(command, args, {files})`, and the page of its `ctx.markdown`) — a page of a megabyte of Cyrillic arrives whole, in the window and the served window alike; more is refused with "too much for one plugin call: 4 MB at most", the command never run; a plugin that isn't installed and on is refused

A plugin reaches git only through `ctx.git` on a folder given to it: `info`, `status`, `log` (a file through its renames) and `show` (a file at a version, capped) with `uses.folders`; `init` and `commit` of exactly the paths it names (the user's other work left as it is; committed by Echo with the plugin's id, authored by the user when git knows them — from their git settings, or the file `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` names in Echo's environment) with `folders.write`. Nothing a repository's settings, hooks or attributes name runs; git found where the system installs it, else on the user's PATH (never in a folder given to a plugin or in Echo's own); git runs only in a repository whose real `.git` folder no plugin can write — one whose history lies outside its folder, a bare repository's files a plugin laid out in its own folder, `core.worktree` set, a partial clone, or settings that read or include a file a plugin could change (there or not; the user's own settings file too, the one `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` names among them, which must be a full path) is refused; no git: said so

A plugin reads Echo's calls as its sheet says (`ctx.echo.read`): `calls` lists them newest first with or without minutes (`{id, title, date, started_at, ended_at, duration_min, app, memo, minutes, transcript, chat, people, participants, threads, client, profile}`; `q` every word in title, folder, subject or people, `since` / `until` (both days in), `thread`, `client`, `limit` 50 up to 500) and `source` of a call also gives its `started_at`, `ended_at`, `duration_min`, `app`, `platform`, `memo`, the invite's `attendees`, its `participants` with the person Echo knows each as (`person`: a key the people read lists, by address, by name only when the invite gives no address; null when none), its meeting `chat` and transcript (each left out with `{chat: false}` / `{transcript: false}`), its threads with their client's name and its `client` (`{id, name}` when its threads have one, else null), and its `minutes` by section, by headings in English, Ukrainian or Russian (`summary`, `decisions`, `questions`, `actions` as Echo keeps them `{id, text, owner, due, done}`, `revision`, `body` without the header); the sheet says "the list of your calls (titles, times, who was invited with their addresses, their threads)" and "your calls' minutes, transcripts, meeting chat and who was invited, …"; a kind it didn't ask for is refused

A plugin reads the meetings Echo last read from the calendar (`ctx.echo.read('calendar', {from, to})`: `{id, subject, start, end, organizer, attendees, join_url, response, threads, client}` — `client` `{id, name}` when its threads have one, `from` / `to` days by its start's local day, no request to Microsoft 365) and who the user is (`'me'`: About me's name and email) as its sheet says ("the meetings Echo has read from your calendar", "your name and email")

A plugin reads the user's About me (Settings → About me) read-only, only with `uses.me: {}` on its sheet ("Reads your About me in Echo (Settings → About me): your name and role, the people and terms of your calls, how you like things written and how you work"; anything but `{}` is refused at check): `ctx.me({kinds})` in its host half gives `null` when About me is missing, empty or still the template, else `{text, name, parts, hash}` — only the parts asked (`identity`, `people`, `terms`, `style`, `patterns`; none named: all but `patterns`), `name` its `Name:` line else Echo's name for the user (with `identity` only), `hash` 8 hex characters that change when what it gets changes; an unknown part throws naming the parts; without `me` on its sheet it is refused ("didn't ask for “me”"); an update that adds it asks again. `ctx.echo.read('me')` stays the user's name and email

A plugin reads the user's Microsoft 365 only through Echo's sign-in and only what `uses.m365.read` names (`mail`, `chats`): `ctx.m365.search`, `ctx.m365.mailThread` (a mail's thread, each message with its attachments' names, never their contents) and `ctx.m365.chat` (a chat's messages on some days); the sheet says what it reads and that it never sends; without Echo's sign-in each says "Microsoft 365 isn't connected"; a kind it didn't ask for (`files` among them) is refused

A plugin with `network.ask` fetches a web address the user types in Echo's own box (`ctx.http.askAddress()`: the system's dialog in Echo's words, never the plugin's page): only that address, only by that plugin, once, a plain GET (no headers or body, no redirect followed), within 10 minutes; a cancelled box gives null, text that isn't an http(s) address is refused; the sheet says "Fetches a web page from an address you type in Echo's own box when it asks — that page only, once each time"; not inside a run Echo started

A plugin puts a chip on a call's row in the calls list (`call.row`: `chip(call)` → a short text, cut at 24 characters, drawn as text with its label as tooltip, in the row's second line); a chip that throws is left out and the list draws; switching the plugin off takes its chips out

A plugin declares its own routines in its manifest (`routines`: id, name, what, a prompt file in its package, every, night, tools, timeout; at most 4, `uses.claude` needed): each is a line of its sheet naming the routine, how often its run comes once the user switches it on, what the run may do (as the routines' setting, its own Auto, skipping every check only with `claude.skip`, or no tools) and its prompt's hash, so an update that changes the routine or its prompt asks again — the user's yes keeping it as they had it, a routine the update adds starting off; a routine breaking a rule refuses the install with why

A plugin's routine is listed with Echo's jobs in the routines' one shape (`echoctl jobs routines`, `ctx.echo.routines`: id `<plugin>.<routine>`, `source` `plugin:<id>`, its every, night and model settings, last run, next run, the month) and in Settings → Plugins on its plugin; it is off until the user switches it on there, on its install or update sheet (F-PLUG-135, F-PLUG-136), on its own setup's offer (F-PLUG-137) or with `echoctl jobs set <id> on=on`, and tuned as Echo's jobs are (`every`, `night`, `model`); a plugin with `uses.echo.jobs` tunes it on the user's click but never switches it on or off

A plugin's routine that is on runs every N minutes while Echo runs (not at night when it pauses then), or now with `echoctl jobs run <id>`, one run at a time: Claude Code on the user's default AI profile (its model setting mapped by the profile) as the folder session, with the prompt its package ships inside Echo's lines (its name, its plugin, its last run), acting on its own as the routines' setting or its own choice says (`skip` only when its sheet has `claude.skip`)

A plugin's routine's runs are recorded as Echo's jobs' are, in Echo's words and counts ("done", the changes and sends it made through Echo, tokens, cost; a failure "the run failed: its log says why"), never the model's text; `echoctl jobs outcome <id> [--run <run>]` gives the user its answer, the changes and sends it made, its mail drafts and its log (a run that failed before Claude Code started too); Echo keeps its last 20 runs' folders

A routine of a plugin that is off doesn't run (`echoctl jobs run` refused, listed not enabled) and keeps the user's settings; removing the plugin switches its routines off; switching a routine on or running one is refused inside a run Echo started

A plugin asks for the microphone with `uses.microphone: {}` (anything else refused at install); its permission sheet says, in Echo's words, that it hears the microphone in its own view only after the user clicks there, with Echo's recording sign on, never while Echo records a call or a memo, stopping when the view is left, and that what it hears can go to the addresses it may reach

A plugin's window half opens the microphone (`ctx.microphone.open`) on the user's click in its own view (its activity or its Knowledge tab) and gets a live audio stream; while it is open the window's top pill reads "<plugin> hears your microphone" with Stop (and the tray shows the recording icon and that line); Stop, `close()`, every track ending, leaving its view, the plugin switched off, updated or removed, or the page loading again stops every track and takes the pill away

A plugin's microphone is refused, with the reason and nothing opened: without the user's click (a timer, an event, its `apply`), outside its own view, for a plugin whose install sheet didn't name `uses.microphone`, while another plugin has it, and while Echo records a call or a memo ("Echo is recording — a plugin gets the microphone once the recording stops"); a recording that starts while a plugin hears the microphone stops it, and the page says so

In the native window (macOS WKWebView, Windows WebView2) the webview gets the microphone only for an opening Echo allowed, once for each; a page's own `getUserMedia` for the microphone outside one, also right after a plugin's microphone stopped, and the camera are refused; a capture no plugin holds is stopped within a second (macOS) or never granted (Windows asks Echo on every request); macOS's own microphone indicator shows while it is open. Screen sharing is not gated by Echo: WKWebView doesn't send `getDisplayMedia` through Echo's permission handler, and WebView2 shows its own picker

A plugin's `ctx.fs.write(…, {createNew: true})` and `ctx.fs.copyIn` make a new file in a folder it was given on a volume without hard links too (exFAT, FAT, many SMB/NFS shares): still never over a file there ("is there already", the file untouched) and no hidden part left

`minutes_written` and `sources_changed` carry what Echo already decided. `minutes_written`: `{id, link, call, stamp, title, started_at, ended_at, duration_min, app, memo, revision, rewritten}` (`rewritten` true when this call's minutes were told before, `revision` changes with the minutes) and, to a plugin that reads sources (`uses.echo.read`: source or sources), also the call's `threads`, `client`, `profile`, `participants` and `minutes` by section — never its transcript. `sources_changed`: `{changed, removed}` ids and, to a reader, `items` (100 at most) with each changed mail's or post's `subject`, `at`, `threads`, `client`, `profile`, `from`, `people` and `trust` as Recall indexed it, and a mail's Microsoft 365 ids as Recall keeps them (`m365_id`: its last message's Graph id, the one `ctx.m365.mailThread` takes; `conversation_id`; null for a post or what Recall didn't keep), never its text; `echo.read('source')` of the same mail or post gives the same routing with Recall's facts per message (`messages: [{from, at, text, link}]`). A plugin that only names the event in `uses.events.on` hears neither routing, people, minutes nor mail subjects and senders

A plugin lists Echo's sources and people with what Echo decided (`ctx.echo.read`): `sources` (`{kind, thread, client, q, since, limit}`) gives calls with minutes `{id, stamp, kind, title, date, threads, client}` and Recall's mail and posts with their subject, day, threads, client, profile, senders, addresses and trust, never a text; `people` gives each person's `aliases`, `email`, `also`, `organisation`, `client` and `key` (what a call's `participants[].person` names), their `places` (`{thread, role, stance}` in each of their open threads) and their reporting line (`reports_to` `{key, name}` or null, `reports` `[{key, name}]`), never a fact or a quote; the sheet's people line says "who the people in your threads are (their names, addresses and organisations)"

A plugin's window half shows a file or folder of a folder the user gave it selected in Finder / Explorer (`ctx.system.reveal(root, path)`, `uses.folders`): only on the user's click or key (else refused with "Finder or Explorer opens only on your click", nothing sent); never outside the folder (`..`, an absolute path, a link out of it), a missing file, a folder it wasn't given, a plugin that didn't ask for folders or is off; never from the host half; on test data only written to the open log (`reveal <path>`)

A plugin's host half reads a web page as Markdown (`ctx.web.read(url, {max, timeout})`, no capability of its own) only where `ctx.http.fetch` may reach — a host its manifest names over https, an address the user listed, a page the user typed once (and, with `uses.network.web`, a public https page: F-PLUG-139) — refused before anything is asked otherwise; a plain GET with no cookies, credentials or redirect followed: {url, title, markdown, links, images, lang, byline, published, description, source, needs_js, truncated, bytes}. The main part without navigation, scripts, forms or frames; headings, lists, code, tables, http(s) links and pictures (`![alt](src)`, a figure's caption under it, tracking pixels and `data:` left out) kept; the page's words never markup and its control and direction marks dropped. A page that builds itself with JavaScript is never run: its JSON-LD, framework state or `<noscript>` text taken when fuller (`source`), `needs_js` when it stays nearly empty. HTML only, never compressed, 5 MB read as it comes, 30 s: a PDF, a redirect ("it moved"), an error status or a page past `max` is refused with why. `ctx.web.markdown(html, {base})` reads HTML the plugin already has the same way, fetching nothing

A plugin saves a page's pictures (`ctx.web.read(url, {images: 'save'})`): each picture gets a file handle {file, name, size, type} in its store's cache (`cache/web/…`, swept with the cache) or the reason it wasn't saved — PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, AVIF or SVG only, 10 MB each, 50 pictures, 50 MB and 2 minutes a page. A picture comes from what the plugin may reach, or — only for a page on the public internet — from its own public host, never from this computer or the user's network; a page on the user's network gets only what the plugin may reach. `ctx.web.fetch(url, {max})` saves one file it may reach (10 MB, up to 50 MB) as a handle

A plugin's window half goes to a hash without a history step (`ctx.go(hash, {replace: true})`): the address changes in place (Back skips it) and the window shows the page as on a hashchange; without `replace`, `ctx.go(hash)` is a history step as before; the hash it is already at only redraws

A plugin gets a call's stamp (`YYYY-MM-DD_HHMMSS`, kept when the call is retitled) as `stamp` wherever it gets a call: the `call` of `call.header`, `call.menu`, `call.minutes` and `call.row`, the `recording_started`, `recording_stopped`, `transcribed` and `minutes_written` events, and the rows of `ctx.echo.read('calls')` and `'sources'`; `ctx.echo.read('source', 'call:<stamp>')` reads the call as its folder's name does (the stamp of no call is refused)

A plugin's Microsoft 365 reads run against a fake Microsoft 365 on this computer in a development build (`ECHOCTL_TEST_GRAPH=http://127.0.0.1:<port>`, `tests/fixtures/fake_graph.py`): Echo counts as signed in with no tokens and sends every Graph request there, so `ctx.m365.search`, `mailThread` and `chat` give the fake's made-up mail and chat; the real sign-in is refused while it is set; a value that isn't a local address leaves Microsoft 365 not connected; a release build never reads it

The system's folder picker a plugin opens (`ctx.system.pickFolder`) lets the user make a new folder in it ("New Folder" on macOS, "Make New Folder" on Windows), and the new folder picked is the one the plugin is given (a new vault in a new folder)

With `uses.folders.write` a plugin writes, appends, makes, moves and removes exactly these hidden names in a folder the user gave it, no sheet line of their own: a `.gitignore` in any folder that isn't hidden, Obsidian's `.obsidian/<name>.json` in any folder that isn't hidden (a vault in a subfolder too; an ASCII name, not `community-plugins.json`, `core-plugins.json` or `core-plugins-migration.json`, in any case: switching an Obsidian plugin on runs its code), and Markdown in a skill of the folder's own Claude Code project, `.claude/skills/<name>/<file>.md` (`<name>` a-z, 0-9, -, up to 64; Markdown that runs nothing — frontmatter only `name`, `description`, `when_to_use`, `argument-hint`, `disable-model-invocation`, `user-invocable`, no `` !` ``, no code block opened with `!`, else refused with "a skill can't run commands"; only written whole, never appended to, copied or moved in; not committed when it fails that; the folders `.obsidian` (in any folder that isn't hidden), `.claude`, `.claude/skills`, `.claude/skills/<name>` made or, empty, removed) — by their exact names and as what a link or short name reaches; everything else hidden is refused ("is hidden"): `.claude/settings*.json`, hooks, agents, commands, anything not `.md` under `.claude` (`SKILL.md.js`), `.Claude`, `.obsidian/plugins` and themes, `.git`, `.mcp.json`; a folder never moved into a hidden place

With `uses.skills: true`, a capability of its own (its sheet line, and no "Runs Claude Code" line unless it also asks for `claude`: "Adds instructions for Claude Code (skills) to your own Claude Code (~/.claude/skills), each only when you click to add it …") a plugin's window half adds a skill to the user's own Claude Code (`ctx.claude.installSkill(name, md)` → `<Claude Code folder>/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` when set) and removes one it added (`ctx.claude.removeSkill(name)`): only on the user's click or key (else refused with "A skill is added to your Claude Code only on your click", nothing sent); never from its host half; Markdown that runs nothing (only `name`, `description`, `when_to_use`, `argument-hint`, `disable-model-invocation`, `user-invocable` in its frontmatter; no `` !` ``, no code block opened with `!`), name a-z, 0-9, - up to 64, 256 KB at most; never over a skill folder there already that it didn't add (the user's, another plugin's); its skills go when it is removed; on test data only into the test's own Claude Code folder

A plugin names a Claude run by a key of its own (`ctx.claude.run({key})`: 1 to 64 letters, digits, `.`, `_` or `-`) and stops it (`await ctx.claude.stop(key)` → true, or false when none of its runs under that key is running): Claude Code and every process it started are stopped (macOS and Windows), wherever the run is (the app or a terminal's `echoctl plugin call`); the pending run fails with `stopped`, its log says "stopped by the plugin" and its record (`permissions.json`) `stopped: true`; a copy run's snapshot goes. A second run under a key still running is refused; a key names only the plugin's own runs (another plugin's run under the same key goes on); a key Echo can't take is refused; stopping needs `uses.claude`

A plugin that asked for it (`uses.echo.read: recording`; the sheet: 'whether Echo is recording or transcribing a call now, and which') reads what Echo records now (`ctx.echo.read('recording')` → {state: idle | recording | transcribing, call, stamp}): `recording` while the watcher records a call or memo, else `transcribing` while a call's transcription runs (the newest), else `idle`; `call` the call's folder name and `stamp` its stamp, both null when idle; a plugin that didn't ask is refused, even one that hears the recording events

A plugin walks its own store as it walks a folder it was given (`await ctx.store.walk(path, {ext, hidden, max, sha})` → [{path, size, mtime, sha?}]): the files under that folder of its store ('' the whole store), paths relative to the store as `ctx.store.read` takes them, off its time slice; dot names left out unless `hidden`, no link followed, nothing outside the store; a folder that isn't there gives []; a path out of the store is refused

A plugin's copy run leaves out of its snapshot what `exclude` names (`ctx.claude.run({folder, mode: 'copy', exclude})`, as `ctx.fs.snapshot`'s: more than 100 refused); `exclude` in another mode or without a folder is refused before Claude Code starts

A plugin's install sheet has a block "Routines — off unless you switch them on" under what it will be able to do: a switch per routine of its manifest with its name, when it runs ("Every N min · paused at night") and what it does, each off as the sheet opens; the routines switched on there are on right after the install, the rest off. An update's sheet shows switches only for the routines the update adds (off) or changes (as the user has it); a routine it keeps unchanged has no switch and stays as the user had it. Each routine's sheet line reads "Has a routine “<name>”, off until you switch it on in Settings → Plugins: then …"

`echoctl plugin install <id> --routines <a,b>|all` and `echoctl plugin update <id> --routines <a,b>|all` switch on the routines named (by their ids; `all`: every routine the sheet offers) once installed; without the flag they stay off as before; the review lists the ids ("Its routines stay off unless you switch them on: --routines a,b (or all)"); a routine the sheet doesn't offer (unknown, or one an update keeps unchanged) is refused, naming the sheet's routines, before anything is installed; `update --routines` without an id is refused

A plugin's client half opens Echo's sheet of its own routines on the user's click (`await ctx.echo.routines.offer(ids?)`, no capability needed): its routines (or those ids), each with Echo's switch, name, when it runs and what it does, and Done; the user switches them there (saved as Settings → Plugins saves them; a click a script makes is ignored), the plugin never; it resolves once the sheet closes to [{id, name, on}]. Without the user's click, or for an id it hasn't, it is refused before the sheet opens

A plugin's JavaScript that runs more than 5 s without an await is stopped, and every call still waiting on that plugin fails at once with "<id>'s job took too long: Echo stops a plugin's JavaScript after 5 s" (#817): `echoctl plugin call` prints it and exits 1, never waiting out its own time limit; the plugin answers its next call as before

A plugin that asks for `uses.speech: true` (its sheet line: "Transcribes audio files you hand it (WAV, webm/opus, ogg/opus, m4a or mp3, up to 60 minutes and 200 MB) with Echo's own speech model, on this computer, or on the transcription server you connected; it starts only while Echo is not recording or transcribing a call. The text goes only to the plugin") transcribes a WAV file it was handed with `ctx.speech.transcribe(file, {words, language})` on Echo's own speech model, in `language` or Settings' first language: `{text, language, segments: [{start, end, text}], words?: [{start, end, word}]}`, the words only when asked and the engine timed them (Whisper, Parakeet and Nemotron do) (#834)

`ctx.speech.transcribe` refuses, with its reason and without waiting: a plugin that didn't ask for `speech`, a file that isn't a handle of its own (a path, another plugin's), a file that isn't a WAV, over 60 minutes of audio or 200 MB, a language Echo doesn't know, no speech model, while Echo records (a call or a memo) or transcribes a call, and while a file is already being transcribed (#834)

A plugin reads the text of a file handed to it with `ctx.files.text(file, {pages, max})` → `{text, pages, truncated}` (#831): PDF (pdfium; `pages` one page or a range, 1-based), Word, PowerPoint, spreadsheets, HTML, Markdown and plain text through Echo's own readers, a file of another name when it has text; `pages` of the answer is a PDF's or deck's page count (`null` otherwise), `truncated` when `max` (1 MB of text, 4 MB at most) cut it; read in a child process killed after 60 s (a crash or hang never reaches Echo), one at a time for a plugin and two in all; a file over 50 MB, an Office file unpacking to over 200 MB or holding over 5000 parts, an old .xls, a file with no text (or an HTML page with almost none), `pages` on a file without pages or past its last page refused with why; no model, no network, no path in the answer, the plugin's own handles only (as `ctx.files.read`), no new line on the sheet

A plugin keeps a file handed to it in its own store with `ctx.store.copyIn(file, path, {createNew})` (#832): the bytes as they are, 50 MB at most, never out of the store, never over Echo's own files there (`settings.json`, `widgets.json`…), never over a file unless `createNew: false`; `ctx.store.usage(dir?)` gives `{bytes, files}` of the store or one of its folders (not `settings.json`)

`ctx.settings.get(key)` gives the manifest's `default` for a setting nobody set (a bool `false` and a number too), what the user set when there is one (an empty string too), and `null` for a setting without a default, a secret (never given a default) or an address list the plugin may reach (#832)

A plugin's window half runs its settings page's connection test with `ctx.call('__testSettings', {section})`: its host half reads the secrets itself, and the window half is given only `{ok, message}` — the message cut at 300 characters, the user's secrets taken out of it, a failure or a plugin without the command told as `{ok: false, message}` (#832)

A plugin with `uses.network.web: true` (its own sheet line "Reads web pages on the public internet (https), and can send what it knows to any site through the addresses it opens"; an update that adds it asks again) reads any https page on the public internet with `ctx.web.read` / `ctx.web.fetch`, with no dialog: port 80 or 443, a host whose every address is public, connected at the address Echo checked and never through a proxy; up to 5 redirects followed, each new address (a relative `Location` against the page it came from) checked again before it is asked — from a public page only as a public page, never into an address the user listed or a host the manifest names. Plain http, another port, this computer, the user's network (private, link-local, unique-local, an IPv4-mapped private address, a name pointing there even in part), a 6th redirect or a redirect to any of these are refused with why. Its other grants keep their rules; without it nothing changes; `ctx.http.fetch` isn't widened; GET only, no cookies or credentials, the same caps (#830)

A plugin's Claude run (`ctx.claude.run`) takes pictures it holds (`images: [handle]`: PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP by their bytes, 10 at most, 3.75 MB each — 5 MB base64-encoded — and 15 MB base64-encoded in all, each the plugin's own handle) with its prompt as one stream-json message on stdin, with `tools: 'none'` too; streams Claude's text as it comes (`onText(chunk)`, gathered 50 ms at most, its text between tool calls too, the result the same); and continues a conversation (`resume`, a run key's characters): its next run resumes the Claude Code session Echo keeps for that plugin and conversation — with no tools in a folder of the plugin's own, so it stays out of the folder session's conversations — refused on another AI profile (both named) or folder than it began on, with `copy`, or once the conversation's pictures would pass 20 or 15 MB; one run at a time; `await ctx.claude.forget(resume)` → true (false when there was none) forgets it with its Claude Code transcript, as removing the plugin with its data does; a session Claude Code no longer has fails the run saying Echo forgot the conversation, and the next run begins a new one. A file that isn't such a picture, one too big, too many, another plugin's handle, or a stream number Echo didn't give is refused before Claude Code starts

`ctx.speech.transcribe` also takes compressed audio — webm/opus (a window's MediaRecorder), ogg (Opus or Vorbis), m4a/mp4 (AAC) and mp3 — read from the file's content, decoded to 16 kHz mono in pure Rust, with the 60-minute cap counted on the decoded audio as it decodes, and a damaged file refused with a reason; one lock (`plugins/.locks/speech.lock`) keeps the app and `echoctl plugin call` to one file at a time (#841)
